title: PostgreSQL connection pool exhaustion on checkout-service causing 504 gateway timeouts
symptoms: 95% of checkout requests timing out at 30s
'dial tcp: i/o timeout' errors in gateway logs
Worker queue depth climbing (Celery workers busy but not progressing)
root_cause: Orphaned Celery workers were holding Redis distributed locks indefinitely after a prior aborted deploy. Long-running tasks never released their lock keys, retries stacked on the same lock records, and every wake-up re-opened a fresh PostgreSQL connection instead of reusing pool sessions. Within minutes the checkout-service pool was saturated and the gateway returned 504s.
resolution_runbook: 1. Rollback the stuck checkout-service deploy: kubectl rollout undo deployment/checkout-service -n production
2. Flush the orphaned Celery Redis lock keys: redis-cli -h <redis-host> --scan --pattern 'locks:celery:*' | xargs redis-cli -h <redis-host> del
3. Raise headroom on the DB pool: psql -c "ALTER SYSTEM SET max_connections = 500; SELECT pg_reload_conf();"
4. Kill stale DB sessions: psql -c "SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state = 'idle' AND state_change < now() - interval '5 minutes' AND pid <> pg_backend_pid();"
5. Re-deploy fixed build with lock timeouts: kubectl set image deployment/checkout-service checkout-service=checkout-service:v1.9.2 -n production
validation: 504 rate back under 0.1%, pool utilisation stable at 180/500, Celery queue depth flat.
